title: How AI Actually Calls an API? Tool Calling Explained from Scratch
why_read: A clear, beginner-friendly explanation of how LLM tool calling actually works under the hood is useful for engineers newer to building LLM applications.
analysis: The article explains that when an LLM 'calls a tool,' it isn't actually executing code itself; it's producing a structured text output requesting a specific function call, which the surrounding application code then executes and feeds the result back into the model. This demystifies a commonly misunderstood mechanism behind AI agents and assistants that can check weather, prices, or dates despite having a fixed training cutoff. It's an introductory-level piece rather than novel research, useful mainly for developers just starting to build with LLM APIs.
